solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Whaler's new boy is in the ocean?

indicators.note: one thing sitting in another means the first word is placed inside the second

parts.note: the ocean is a body of water
taken as written

explanation.surface: A question about where a whaling ship's newest recruit has ended up: overboard?
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits 'in the ocean' is not where the boy really is; the definition is the specialist Chambers sense of a whaling hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers records a waister as a raw or broken-down hand on a whaling vessel, stationed amidships in the waist.

clue.text: Welsh nurse finds bear

parts.note: W is the standard abbreviation for Welsh
to nurse someone is to help them

explanation.surface: A Welsh nurse comes across a bear, perhaps in a zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, but it is the verb meaning to give birth.
explanation.definitionFit: To whelp is to give birth to puppies or cubs, so it is a specific sense of bearing young.

clue.text: General is regrouping pirates as before

indicators.note: regrouping a set means putting its members into a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A military commander is reorganising his forces, as he did before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As before' marks the sense as old: Algerine was once the usual name for a Barbary pirate.
explanation.definitionFit: Algerines, natives of Algiers, were historically notorious corsairs, so the word formerly served for pirates generally.

clue.text: In grand gown daughter walks making entrance

indicators.note: someone who walks out leaves, so that letter departs from the word

parts.note: taken as written
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
a gown is a dress
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter in a grand gown makes her entrance down the stairs.
explanation.walkthrough: D for daughter is removed from DRESS, leaving RESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingress is a formal word for the act of going in, an entry or entrance.

clue.text: Kensington Gardens, wherein you'll get natural pain relief

indicators.note: wherein says the thing sought lies within the preceding words

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A London park is offered as a place to find natural pain relief.
explanation.walkthrough: Kensington Gardens is a royal park in London.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonga is a Fijian medicinal preparation from plant bark, once used as a remedy for neuralgia.

clue.text: Basque has this — blooming great, I have chest

indicators.note: blooming as a mild British intensifier also suggests something opening out into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
the contraction I've
a chest is a case for storing things

explanation.surface: Someone boasting about their great chest, with a nod to the Basque people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' reads as a mild expletive; it signals the shuffle. The definition is a description: Basque is the classic ergative language.
explanation.definitionFit: Basque grammar marks the subject of a transitive verb with a special form, the ergative case.

clue.text: Reprobate objecting to acting

parts.note: rep is a short form of reprobate in Chambers
resenting something is objecting to it

explanation.surface: A rogue who disapproves of the theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To' links objecting with acting in the surface, but cryptically it just joins wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawyer or agent representing a client is acting on their behalf, so the two participles match.

clue.text: Your tip for marinade? Eastern herb

parts.note: the old form of your

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its very end point, here taken as its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of the word
E is the abbreviation for Eastern

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: add an eastern herb to the marinade.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is a common culinary herb of the mint family, often used in marinades.

clue.text: Celebrity succeeded going down with what Ivan had?

indicators.note: the moved letter ends up placed among the remaining ones, one step further along
in a down entry, going down means that letter leaves its place and moves lower

parts.note: stardom is celebrity, the state of being famous
S is the abbreviation for succeeded

explanation.surface: A famous figure's success falling away, in the time of Ivan the Terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: The S of STARDOM drops one place in the down light, giving TSARDOM.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivan the Terrible was the first ruler crowned Tsar of Russia, so he held a tsardom; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Chasséing odd bits from white male leaves standard language

indicators.note: chassé suggests the French chasser, to chase off, so the odd-numbered characters are sent away

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

explanation.surface: A dancing white man shuffles away from an established language.
explanation.walkthrough: A chassé is a gliding ballroom step, the dance picture hiding the instruction to chase away letters.
explanation.definitionFit: HTML is the standard markup language in which web pages are written.

clue.text: Vigorous mum who's flush and likely to blow up?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a young affluent parent, on the pattern of yuppie
second meaning: prone to shrill barking, as a small dog is

explanation.walkthrough: Flush means rich here, and vigorous hints at youth; the second sense is a stretch, as yapping is a sudden noisy outburst.
explanation.definitionFit: Yappy is both a coinage for a young affluent parent and an adjective for a dog given to noisy barking.

clue.text: Title 'eard in 'Amburg during General Staff's early wanderings

indicators.note: the apostrophes show dropped aitches, so the word is said without its opening letter

parts.note: Herr is the German title for Mr
in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: early points to the opening letters of the two words

parts.note: the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: A German officer's title overheard in Hamburg while the general staff wander about.
explanation.walkthrough: HERR loses its aitch, as the clue's own spelling does, to give ERR.
explanation.definitionFit: Erring is going astray, so errings are acts of straying or wandering from the right path.

clue.text: Sylvan spread is what gets teuchters up

parts.note: sylvan means of woods; here it stands for woodland itself
to air news is to broadcast or spread it

explanation.surface: A woodland spread, as a picnic feast for Highland folk.
explanation.walkthrough: Teuchter is a Lowland Scots term for a Highlander or country person.
explanation.definitionFit: A forestair is a Scottish outside staircase at the front of a house, which is how such people get up.

clue.text: Marking crib score without quietly bombing?

indicators.note: without says the following item is to be left out

parts.note: cribbage points are marked by moving pegs on a board
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A cribbage player keeping score silently, until something goes off.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the P from PEGGING leaves EGGING.
explanation.definitionFit: Egging is pelting someone with eggs, a jokey form of bombarding them, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Jack, a baby

parts.note: pam is the knave, or jack, of clubs in the card game loo
a as in 'ten pounds a head', meaning per

explanation.surface: Jack is described as a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baby' is a verb here, not the infant.
explanation.definitionFit: To baby someone is to treat them indulgently, which is to pamper them.

clue.text: Lesson in role reversal

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A teaching moment in which the pupil and the teacher swap places.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reversal' tempts a backwards reading, but the letters read forwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Lere is an old Spenserian word for learning or a lesson, related to lore.

clue.text: Poets who could be political moderates making take over

indicators.note: making one thing into another says one letter is turned into a different one

parts.note: centrists hold the middle ground in politics
R, recipe, is the abbreviation for take in prescriptions
O is the cricket abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: Poets who might also be moderate politicians, taking control.
explanation.walkthrough: The R in CENTRISTS becomes O.
explanation.definitionFit: A cento is a poem patched together from lines of other poets, and centoists are the writers who compose them.

clue.text: Track down and feed off commie in Intelligence

indicators.note: in places the preceding word inside the following one

parts.note: the pate is the head, seat of intelligence
a red is a communist

explanation.surface: A spy agency hunts down a communist mole and lives off him.
explanation.walkthrough: Intelligence suggests a spy service, but it is the head.
explanation.definitionFit: To predate is to act as a predator: hunting prey and eating it.

clue.text: Most valued prof, eg, is put on to entertain you, biblically

indicators.note: a host who entertains takes a guest inside the house

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on
the archaic plural you of the Bible

explanation.surface: A treasured professor puts on a show to entertain the reader in biblical style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prof, eg' looks like it gives DON; instead don comes from 'put on', and prof is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A doyen is the most senior and respected member of a group, such as an eminent professor.

clue.text: Slight old maid checking lad playing — it's liberating

indicators.note: checking means holding back or restraining, so one part is held within the other

parts.note: dis or diss means to slight, show disrespect
a prim, fussy person, the stereotype of an old maid
a son is a lad
in cricket a batsman in is playing

explanation.surface: An old maid scolds a boy at play, which somehow sets him free.
explanation.walkthrough: An old maid here is the stereotype of a prim, censorious person; in cricket a batsman who is in is playing. Definition and answer are both present participles.
explanation.definitionFit: To disprison is an old verb for releasing from prison, so disprisoning is literally liberating.

clue.text: End last month calm

parts.note: December is the last month of the year
to calm someone is to ease their mind

explanation.surface: A wish that the last month of the year may end calmly.
explanation.definitionFit: Decease is a formal word for death, the end of a life.

clue.text: Bastion once right for very demanding highbinder

indicators.note: one letter for another means the first takes the place of the second

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for right
V is the abbreviation for very
a vampire is an extortioner who bleeds people, and highbinder is an American word for a swindler or gangster

explanation.surface: A fortress for an exacting gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: In VAMPIRE, R replaces V.
explanation.definitionFit: Rampire is an obsolete form of rampart, a defensive earth wall or bastion.

clue.text: By injection these aid infection protection in eye mostly

definitions.text: By injection these aid infection protection

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the final letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
ocular is a facetious noun for the eye

explanation.surface: A medical note: injected substances help protect the eye against infection.
explanation.walkthrough: OCULAR loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Inocula, plural of inoculum, are the material injected in vaccination to build up immunity.

clue.text: Sense TV name squirming about Liberal's acts of bondage

indicators.note: about means around, so the wriggled letters surround what follows
squirming is wriggling and twisting about, so the letters move into new places

parts.note: taken as written
L is the abbreviation for Liberal

explanation.surface: A TV personality writhes at a Liberal politician's bondage habits.
explanation.definitionFit: Enslavements are acts of reducing people to slavery, putting them in bondage.

clue.text: Coloured chilli sauce back inside of American guts to a degree

parts.note: C is an abbreviation for coloured

indicators.note: back means the word is read in the backward direction

parts.note: mole is a Mexican sauce of chilli and chocolate

explanation.surface: Hot sauce that turns an American's insides a different colour, somewhat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To a degree' only softens the definition: the celom is the cavity around the gut, so it is the gut's inside loosely speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Celom is the American spelling of coelom, the body cavity of an animal in which the gut lies.

clue.text: Subject in history such as fiction contains

indicators.note: one item containing another holds it inside

parts.note: a lie is a fiction
e.g., for example

explanation.surface: History as a subject, with fiction in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subject' looks like a school subject; it is a vassal, a feudal subject.
explanation.definitionFit: In feudal times a liege was a vassal owing allegiance, a subject bound to a lord.

clue.text: Obscure engraving on oar's shaft

parts.note: eng. is the abbreviation for engraving
the loom of an oar is its shaft, the part inboard of the blade

explanation.surface: An unclear engraving found on the shaft of an oar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' reads as an adjective but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To engloom is to make gloomy or dark, which is to obscure something.

clue.text: Soul so lacking in quiet place of detention

indicators.note: in puts what is left inside the next word

parts.note: to gag someone is to make them quiet

indicators.note: lacking something means doing without it, so those letters go

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A spirit, lacking much, finds itself in a quiet prison.
explanation.walkthrough: SOUL without SO is UL, which goes into GAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The gulag was the Soviet system of forced-labour camps, used for any such prison camp.

clue.text: Old Swahilis appear to rise invaded by Zulu

indicators.note: rising in a down light means reading from the bottom up
something invaded has another thing get inside it

parts.note: to appear is to seem
Zulu is Z in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Elderly East Africans seem to rise up when invaded by Zulus.
explanation.walkthrough: SEEM reversed is MEES, with Z inserted after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Mzee is a Swahili term of respect for an elder, an old man.

clue.text: Woopie left in school

indicators.note: in puts the preceding letter inside the following word

parts.note: a gam is a school of whales
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A well-off older person left at school.
explanation.definitionFit: Glam (greying, leisured, affluent, married) and woopie (well-off older person) are near-equivalent acronyms for comfortable older people.

clue.text: Science, unknown to wit in short form

parts.note: sci. is the abbreviation for science
z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Science, unknown to the clever, put in brief.
explanation.definitionFit: Sciz is an abbreviation of the Latin scilicet, namely, the same meaning as viz.

clue.text: Abraham Lincoln's foremost couple accepted garden ornament

parts.note: Abe is the short form of Abraham

indicators.note: the foremost couple are the front pair of the word's characters

parts.note: the first two letters
A is the abbreviation for accepted

explanation.surface: The first couple, the Lincolns, accept a garden ornament.
explanation.definitionFit: Abelia is a flowering shrub grown as an ornamental plant in gardens.

clue.text: Punishment that is about lines and you and I

indicators.note: about means around, so the outer word surrounds what follows

parts.note: i.e., id est, that is
L for line, doubled for the plural
you and I together are us

explanation.surface: A schoolroom: lines given as punishment to both of us.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lines' suggests the school punishment, but here they are only letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill-use, as a noun, is cruel or harsh treatment, which can amount to punishment.

clue.text: One of your Greens who's fired with lively energy

parts.note: Alan Sugar, the British TV boss of The Apprentice, famous for 'You're fired!'; the link to firing is loose
snap is liveliness or vigour

explanation.surface: A Green Party member sacked for being too energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: Greens suggests a political party, but it means green vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: The sugar snap is a variety of pea with an edible pod, eaten as a green vegetable.

clue.text: Body-swerving trustee end for release of old Scots

indicators.note: to body-swerve something is to dodge it, so those letters are avoided

parts.note: the extreme of something is its furthest end
TR is the abbreviation for trustee

explanation.surface: A trustee dodging their role in the end, freeing old Scots.
explanation.walkthrough: EXTREME without TR leaves EXEME.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeme is an old Scots word meaning to exempt or release.

clue.text: The intellegentsia, say, matter after gallons

parts.note: e.g., for example, as 'say' can mean
G is the abbreviation for gallons
mass is matter, the stuff a body is made of

explanation.surface: Intellectuals think matter is more important than gallons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts MASS behind G. The clue misspells intelligentsia.
explanation.definitionFit: Egg mass is a colloquial collective term for the eggheads or intellectuals of a society.
